newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore rubber ends down in thin, flat trade.
newsitem.headline: Singapore rubber ends down in thin, flat trade.

text.p: Rubber futures finished lower across the board on Thursday in extremely thin trade with most of the action focused on light buying for RSS3 rubber, dealers said.

"The moderate buying we saw yesterday failed to repeat itself. We only saw very small tonnages of RSS3 rubber being bought while the volume for the other rubber grades were almost non-existent," a trader in a foreign brokerage house said.
"I have not done anything today. It was a very, very quiet market. Aside from buying for RSS3 rubber, there was nothing else going in the market," another rubber trader said.
The total volume traded for RSS3 rubber reached a little over 2,800 tonnes. One forward shipment of RSS1 rubber was traded while TSR20 rubber was untraded for the day, dealers said.
At around 0945 GMT, April RSS3 was seen at 120.00-122.00 U.S. cents a kg from the previous 122.25 cents.
April RSS1 was indicated at 172.50 Singapore cents (US$1.21) a kg from the previous 173.50 cents.
April TSR20 was indicated at 168.00-169.00 Singapore cents (US$1.18-$1.19) a kg from yesterday's 169.00 cents.
